services.name: Kitchen Renovations

leader.cta_line: A kitchen is plumbing, electrical and waterproofing behind cabinetry. Get the order wrong and the finishes pay for it.

services.intro_body:
Kitchen renovations in Cape Town are decided by the services, not the doors. Sinks, hob positions, plug points and the fall of the waste pipe set the layout long before a worktop is chosen.

We plan the room around what is already in the walls, strip out, do the plumbing and electrical first fix, then fit cabinetry, worktops, tiling and finishes with one team. If the layout changes, we say what that costs honestly, because moving a drain is a different job to replacing doors.

services.name: Bathroom Renovations

leader.cta_line: A bathroom is the one room where a shortcut behind the tiles costs more than the tiles did.

services.intro_body:
Bathroom renovations in Cape Town live or die on waterproofing and fall. Water that cannot drain away from the shower finds the wall, the ceiling below and the adjacent room, usually a year after the job looked finished.

We strip to structure, rebuild the falls, waterproof, flood test, then tile and fit. It is slower than tiling over what is there, and it is the difference between a bathroom that lasts and one that gets redone.

services.name: Home Renovations

leader.cta_line: Renovation contractors are judged on the sequencing. Structure and services first, finishes last, in that order.

services.intro_body:
Home renovations in Cape Town range from one room to a whole house, and the difference in cost is rarely the finishes. It is whether walls move, whether the electrical and plumbing need replacing, and how much of the house is live while the work happens.

We survey, check the structure rather than assume it, write a scope with sections priced separately, and phase the work so you can keep living in part of the house. Extensions, open-plan changes and full refurbishments all run on that sequence.

services.name: Waterproofing Durbanville

leader.cta_line: Durbanville roofs take the north-westerly front first. That is why the leaks start on the western elevation.

services.intro_body:
Waterproofing in Durbanville is mostly about wind-driven rain on the western and northern faces, and about walls that stay damp because water sits against them. Older properties in the area often have parapets and box gutters detailed before the materials we use now, and newer estates have flat roofs and balconies with the same junction problems.

We work across Durbanville from Goodwood, trace the entry point, and specify for the substrate. Roofs, parapets, balconies and damp wall bases are all handled by the same team.

services.name: Painters Durbanville

leader.cta_line: Exterior paint in Durbanville takes sun on one face and driving rain on the other. Preparation decides which one wins.

services.intro_body:
Painters in Durbanville work on walls that are chalky, cracked or holding damp that has been painted over before. Paint applied to a damp or unprepared wall fails within two winters, usually on the elevation that takes the weather.

We wash, scrape and repair first, treat damp at its source, then use a coating system matched to the surface. Interior work is done room by room with daily clean-up, so the house stays usable.

services.name: Waterproofing Somerset West

leader.cta_line: Older Somerset West homes were built before the membranes we use now. The junctions are where they leak.

services.intro_body:
Waterproofing in Somerset West runs into older construction: slate and timber roofs, parapets without upstands, gutters sized for a different rainfall. Add wind off the Helderberg and water gets pushed into places a coating will not reach.

We inspect the roof, gutters and wall junctions, trace where the water actually enters, and specify a repair that suits the age of the building rather than covering it in a modern product that traps moisture.

services.name: Waterproofing Southern Suburbs

leader.cta_line: Southern suburbs rain sits on the mountain side of the house. Cellars, boundary walls and old roofs take it first.

services.intro_body:
Waterproofing in Cape Town's southern suburbs deals with older housing stock, steep sites and walls that hold water against them through winter. Cellars, under-house storage and boundary walls on a slope are common, and each fails differently.

We inspect, trace the water to its entry point, and choose between positive-side treatment, drainage and replastering depending on what is actually reachable. Where we cannot get to the wet side, we say so and design for the dry side instead.
